The edition's own statement of rights (from eBible.org's page for this
translation):
> "King James Version + Apocrypha
The King James Version or Authorized Version of the Holy Bible, using the standardized text of 1769, with Apocrypha/Deuterocanon
Public Domain
Language: English
Dialect: archaic British

Letters patent issued by King James with no expiration date means that to print this translation in the United Kingdom or import printed copies into the UK, you need permission. Currently, the Cambridge University Press, the Oxford University Press, and Collins have the exclusive right to print this Bible translation in the UK. This royal decree has no effect outside of the UK, where this work is firmly in the Public Domain. Please see http://www.cambridge.org/about-us/who-we-are/queens-printers-patent and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_James_Version#Copyright_status for more information.

This free text of the King James Version of the Holy Bible is brought to you courtesy of the Crosswire Bible Society and eBible.org."

Why this is public domain:
The King James Version was first published in 1611; the text used is the standardised 1769 Oxford (Blayney) edition. Everyone who made it died centuries ago, so it is public domain in the United Kingdom (its country of origin) and in the United States. eBible.org notes that the United Kingdom letters patent over printing the KJV is a printing monopoly held by licensed printers, not a copyright, and that outside the UK the work is firmly in the public domain.

The read-aloud archive holds the Bible text chapter by chapter as plain
text, a front file, the copyright page (copr.htm, left out of the source),
and eBible.org's signing key (keys.asc, left out).

Sources of these facts: eBible.org's details page
(https://ebible.org/details.php?id=eng-kjv) and the edition's own files.
